life_summary: Moses Thatcher was born on February 2, 1842, in Sangamon County, Illinois, during the early period of Latter-day Saint settlement in the Midwest. He grew up within the Church community and received his basic education before the Thatcher family relocated to Utah Territory as part of the great exodus of Mormon pioneers. As a young man, Thatcher became known for his dedication to community service and his willingness to take on responsibility. He developed a reputation as a thoughtful and principled leader, qualities that would define his long tenure in Church leadership. Throughout his life, he remained engaged in both ecclesiastical and civic affairs in Utah Territory.
church_summary: Moses Thatcher served as a missionary beginning at age 15, completing his first mission in 1858, and later served in the United Kingdom and France (1866-1868) and as a mission president in Mexico (1879-1880). He was ordained as an apostle in April 1879 and served in the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles until 1896, when he was removed over disagreement regarding church control of public office-seeking. He remained in good standing and retained his apostolic priesthood office until his death in 1909 at age 67. He also served as second assistant to Wilford Woodruff in the Young Men's Mutual Improvement Association from 1880 to 1898.
